seoTitle: Nmap Output Analyzer: Open Ports, Services and Risk Notes
metaDescription: Paste nmap normal or grepable output for a table of open ports per host, risky exposures such as RDP, SMB, Redis or Docker, and outdated versions.
intro: Make nmap results readable: open ports per host, risky services highlighted, old software versions noted.
why:
Nmap output is accurate but long. This analyser reads normal (-oN) and grepable (-oG) formats, builds a table of open ports with service and version per host, lists other states, and adds notes from a built-in list of risky ports (telnet, SMB, RDP, VNC, databases, Redis, Elasticsearch, Docker API, memcached) and a few outdated-version patterns in banners.

The notes are generic hints by port number and banner text. They are not vulnerability findings: confirm each service, patch level and exposure. Only scan systems you own or are authorised to test.
howTo: Run nmap with -oN or -oG and copy the file contents.
Review each host table and the notes underneath.

faq.a: No. A web page cannot send raw packets. It only reads results you already have.

faq.q: Are the risk notes a vulnerability scan?
faq.a: No. They flag services that are commonly exposed by mistake and software that is old by version number.
Not yet. Use -oN or -oG, or convert with xsltproc.
